subject: Re: Northbridge - On‑Prem BYOK / Operator Access Alignment
messages:
From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@northbridge.health>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; privacy-team@northbridge.health
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑Prem deployment: BYOK and operator access questions

Karthik — thanks for the demo last week. The security team asked for clarity on three items before we sign the DPA addendum: 

1) Operator access: we need a clear list of the circumstances under which Redwood engineers would be able to access the on‑prem instance (if any).
2) Key custody: we plan to use our HSM and customer‑managed keys (BYOK). Please confirm whether Redwood will ever hold unencrypted copies of keys, and whether key escrow is required.
3) Data egress: we need to understand any telemetry or troubleshooting artifacts that would leave our VPC.

I've attached our initial redlines to the DPA for context. Can we get a short runbook or matrix that maps operator actions to required approvals? Ideally we want this by EOD next Wednesday since procurement needs timing for their review cycle.

—Daniel
Director, InfoSec
Northbridge Health

Attachment: northbridge_dpa_redlines_v1.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@northbridge.health>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai; sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑Prem deployment: BYOK and operator access questions

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step: 

1) Operator access: Redwood does not have routine operator access to customer VPCs. We only request access for a narrow set of scenarios: (a) critical incident response where customer systems are unavailable, (b) platform security incident requiring coordinated triage, or (c) mutually agreed onboarding tasks (e.g., assisted install). Access in those cases is controlled by a documented break‑glass process and logged.

2) Key custody: For the on‑prem package we support BYOK with customer HSMs. Redwood never holds plaintext keys. We can support a key‑escrow option but only if explicitly requested and with mutually agreed escrow controls.

3) Data egress: By default, no application data leaves the VPC. We may collect minimal telemetry (service liveness, error rates, sizes/timings) if enabled; we can make telemetry opt‑in and provide the exact telemetry schema. No model artifacts or customer payloads are sent to Redwood High‑Trust systems unless you enable a remote troubleshooting bundle.

Next step: Irene (cc'd) is our lead for DPA and operator entitlements. Irene — can you prepare an operator entitlements matrix and a 1‑page break‑glass runbook for Northbridge? We will target a draft by Tue, 2026‑04‑06. Daniel — does that timeline work?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@northbridge.health>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: On‑Prem deployment: BYOK and operator access questions

Daniel — attaching the draft matrix and a short runbook. Summary below and a few clarifying questions embedded in the matrix.

Summary (high level):
- Routine ops: no Redwood access. All node management and keystore ops are performed by customer admins.
- Assisted onboarding: temporary, timeboxed access via ephemeral VPN jumpbox; requires signed approval from your onboarding owner and a scheduled 1‑hour window.
- Escalation/incident: break‑glass requires (i) signed approval from an authorized Northbridge approver (list per matrix), (ii) two‑factor token from Redwood SRE, and (iii) session capture (screen + command audit) uploaded to your S3 bucket (or retained in‑VPC if you prefer).
- Key handling: Redwood will only perform cryptographic operations on keys that remain in your HSM; we will never export plaintext keys. If you prefer, we can deploy a redis‑based KV cache with encrypted pointers, but keys remain under your KMS.

Open clarifications in the matrix (row references):
- Q3: If we are asked to run a remote diagnostics bundle that includes logs with partial user content, do you prefer (A) an air‑gapped upload area under your control, or (B) a time‑limited upload to a Redwood staging bucket encrypted by your public key?
- Q6: For escrow — do you have a preferred legal recipient and escrow provider? If not, we can propose one used by other healthcare customers.

I've attached: operator_entitlements_matrix.xlsx and a short PDF runbook. If that looks ok we'll incorporate your feedback into the DPA redlines and a one‑page schedule to append to the addendum.

—Irene
Legal and Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator_entitlements_matrix.xlsx

From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@northbridge.health>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; ops@acmecloud.com; privacy-team@northbridge.health
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑Prem deployment: BYOK and operator access questions

Irene / Karthik — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we were looking for. A couple quick items: 

- Opt‑in telemetry: please make telemetry disabled by default in the installer. We'll enable if we need it.
- Diagnostics bundle: option (A) — an air‑gapped area under our control.
- Escrow: we'll review with legal but prefer to avoid escrow unless required by procurement; we'll loop legal on that thread separately.

Timeline: final DPA redline feedback from procurement (with these matrices attached) by Friday 2026‑04‑09 is ideal. If you can land the matrices with the DPA schedule by tomorrow EOD we can keep to that schedule.

We'll also expect that any break‑glass requires at minimum two named approvers from Northbridge (we'll provide the list).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Daniel
Director, InfoSec
Northbridge Health

Forwarded message headers preserved for the record.
